bestseller = a book that sells in very large numbers
sequel = a book or film that continues an earlier story
prequel = a story set before the events of the original
autobiography = a book a person writes about their own life
biography = a book about another person's life, written by someone else
memoir = a personal account of a period in the writer's life
satire = writing that uses humour to criticise people or institutions
metaphor = a figure of speech that describes something as if it were something else
protagonist = the main character in a story
antagonist = the character who opposes the main character
narrator = the voice that tells the story
plot twist = a sudden, surprising change in the story
cliffhanger = an ending that leaves the audience waiting to know what happens
anthology = a collection of poems, stories or extracts by different writers
prose = ordinary written language, not poetry
sonnet = a fourteen-line poem with a set rhyme pattern
fable = a short story, often with animals, that teaches a moral
allegory = a story whose characters and events stand for ideas
irony = a contrast between what is said or expected and what is meant or happens
theme = a central idea that a work of art explores
